newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea parliament opens probe on president's son.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea parliament opens probe on president's son.

text.p: South Korea's parliament on Monday started a week of hearings on the alleged role of President Kim Young-sam's son in a loans scandal and in state affairs.

Opposition lawmakers have accused the president's second son, Kim Hyun-chul, of taking kickbacks over a business deal involving the troubled Hanbo Group and of meddling in government appointments and policy decisions.
They also alleged that Hyun-chul indirectly pressured banks to provide massive loans to Hanbo's steelmaking flagship in excess of its collateral.
The special committee probing the loans scandal that surfaced after the collapse in January of Hanbo Steel Co questioned Park Kyung-shik, Hyun-chul's doctor.

Park, who last month released a video tape showing Hyun-chul discussing the appointment for the head of a state-backed cable news company, told a hearing on Monday that he believed Hyun-chul illegally meddled in state affairs.
Park said he had evidence that Hyun-chul pressured the government in connection with health-related legislation.
The committee is due to question two close associates of Hyun-chul, including a former intelligence official, before questioning the president's son on Friday.
State prosecutors have said they are separately probing allegations involving Hyun-chul, but denied reports by local media that they have found enough evidence to charge him.
The collapse of Hanbo Steel Co under $5.8 billion of loans led to the arrest of 11 people, including close aides to President Kim, Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo, and bankers and politicians.

The president apologised in February for a furore caused by the Hanbo scandal and reshuffled his cabinet. He said he was shamed that his son was implicated in the scandal and said Hyun-chul must be punished if any wrongdoing was uncovered.
Hyun-chul was exonerated by the prosecution after questioning in February in connection with Hanbo, but the opposition called the prosecution probe a whitewash.
The opposition seized on Park's tape as a smoking gun and demanded a reopening of the investigation into Hanbo.
A renewed prosecution probe has led to the questioning of more than 30 politicians, including National Assembly speaker Kim Soo-han and the mayor of South Korea's second largest city.
Most have admitted receiving "political funds" from Hanbo but denied that any favours were returned.
